title: ELECTION INTERFERENCE: The shocking truth about AI deepfakes in politics
description: Send us Fan Mail In this eye-opening episode of 'Preparing for AI', we dive into the controversial world of AI-driven election interference. We explore the shocking findings from Channel 4's investigation 'Can AI Steal Your Vote?', which revealed how AI-generated content swayed 23 out of 25 voters in just two weeks. We break down the potential threats of deepfakes, AI-generated robocalls, and social media manipulation, while also discussing the opportunities AI presents for improving election administration and cybersecurity. From Sunak to Biden, Trump to Trudeau, we examine how AI is reshaping political landscapes globally. We also look at policy responses from governments and tech companies, and offer practical advice for voters, candidates, and election officials on navigating this new digital frontier of democracy. Join us as we unravel the complex relationship between AI and elections, and learn how to protect your vote in an era of digital deception. The Truth About AI's Impact on Politics (Channel 4 documentary) https://youtu.be/7vXlBZlV7Ks?si=mYAVh8MRXiXXM5nk Election Related AI Deepfakes Spread Across India's Social Media (NBC News) https://youtu.be/LIPkDso-uHA?si=ce7-G0R8_VAh96KR
summary: Reacting to Channel 4's 'Can AI Steal Your Vote?', Matt and Jimmy dissect how a fake social app fed deepfakes of Sunak and Starmer to 25 voters and swayed 23 of them within two weeks — often with a single targeted fear like a £35 GP charge. They widen the lens to AI-cloned news anchors in India, a Kate Middleton imprisonment deepfake circulating on WeChat, and the collapse of trustable evidence, landing on practical defences: read manifestos, think critically, and get off social media before elections.
keyTalkingPoints: Channel 4 experiment: 23 of 25 voters swung by AI-generated content in two weeks via the fake 'Echo' app
One well-targeted sentence (NHS £35 charge, immigrants atop housing lists) was enough to flip most participants
India: cloned news-anchor deepfakes produced in hours, in multiple languages, all accepted and published on YouTube
China: a fake Kate Middleton 'imprisoned by William' video was allowed through censorship to brew as clickbait
Even after debunks, anger persists — the 'synapse is already rewired'; confirmation bias beats corrections
Defences: read party manifestos directly, critical thinking, avoid social media before elections, Ground News slider

jimmy: Even AI-aware viewers can be fooled by good deepfakes, and the unaware have no reason to doubt them
Mainstream media has so far debunked big deepfakes quickly, but lower-profile races and swing states are the real risk
The answer is critical thinking and questioning everything online — tiring, but the alternative is being sold a lie
For elections specifically, people should read manifestos and watch debates rather than trust clips
matt: Evidence itself is no longer believable — we are in a 'post post-truth' world staring at 99%-real fakes
He does not trust fact-checkers or mainstream media in general; only self-verification and manifestos
Companies and states will steer even innocent joke deepfakes once they go viral, as China's censors did
Admits he has been struggling for months to know what to believe and recommends steering clear of social media
